description: Order header. id joins order_items.order_id, payments.order_id and refunds.order_id. Only status='completed' counts toward gross/net revenue. Dates are UTC YYYY-MM-DD. Net revenue is completed-order line-item sales minus succeeded refunds, attributed to order_date. Aggregate refunds per order before joining. Revenue without gross/net is ambiguous: ask for clarification. Do not join payments to line items for revenue.

One row per order line. order_items.order_id joins orders.id; product_id joins products.id. Gross revenue is SUM(quantity * unit_price_cents) for completed orders. All money is integer INR cents (paise); divide by 100 for rupees. Multiple items and multiple refunds must be aggregated separately to avoid fanout.

Multiple refunds may exist per order. Only status='succeeded' reduces net revenue. Ignore pending refunds. refunds.order_id joins orders.id. Aggregate amount_cents per order before joining to line-item sales. Amounts are INR cents. Net-revenue refunds are grouped by the original order date.

Product dimension. products.id joins order_items.product_id. Category and name support product sales analysis. Product rankings use gross completed-order sales unless the question specifies a different definition.
Synthetic customer dimension containing only id, segment, and region. customers.id joins orders.customer_id. No names, emails, phone numbers, or real personal data are stored.

Payment attempts/captures, potentially multiple per order. status='captured' means collected; void payments are excluded. Captured payments are not the revenue definition. Never join payments directly with order_items to calculate revenue because the join duplicates line-item amounts.
